top_story: Israel’s punitive operation in Hebron escalated on 23–24 October from demolitions after a gunfight that killed two soldiers into the forced eviction of hundreds of Palestinian families, tightening a pattern of collective punishment that deepens displacement and civilian insecurity in the occupied West Bank. In Sudan, the humanitarian collapse in El-Fasher has become even starker, with Amnesty assessing the city’s population at just seven percent of last year’s high after the UAE-backed Rapid Support Forces seized it amid killings, torture, and disappearances. These late-October shocks land atop an older but still dangerous regional baseline set in March, when US threats against Iran’s power grid drew Tehran’s vow of wider escalation tied to the Strait of Hormuz. The regional picture is one of coercive power being applied against civilian spaces, with immediate human devastation in Hebron and El-Fasher and persistent risk that unresolved interstate confrontation could widen that harm across the region.
